vab mhg k71, "kolbe, john gerson eleazar. eggenote anna jacoba (gebore van der merwe)", 1868. and the mccabe name is already in this archive: a rosa magdalena kolbe was baptised at bloemfontein in 1890 to frederik fortuna kolbe and maria petronella elizabeth antoinetta mccabe - a second kolbe-mccabe marriage in the same small free state world, and this archive does not yet know whether that is a coincidence. 20 september 2026 - it may not be one. on a geni profile, the frederik fortunata kolbe of that baptism is the commandant's own son, born 1857 at bloemfontein - so the commandant's widow married francis mccabe the landdrost about april 1871, and her son married a mccabe. mccabe died ten months later leaving "four sons and two daughters, besides a large family of step-children". the two households were one for eleven months, and a marriage across them afterwards is ordinary rather than remarkable. and this archive already held the other half without noticing. vab mhg c129, the 1872 estate index for francis mccabe, names his first wife as maria petronella elisabetha antoinetta raath - and the bloemfontein baptism of 1890 names the mother as maria petronella elizabeth antoinetta mccabe. the same four-part name, carrying mccabe as a surname: she is almost certainly his daughter by raath, named for her mother entire. so a stepbrother married a stepsister, nine years after their parents' eleven-month marriage, and mccabe's obituary had already said he left "four sons and two daughters, besides a large family of step-children". the one link that is from a user tree and not from a document is that her husband is the commandant's son; it is not adopted, and vab mhg c129 would settle it by naming the daughters. neither estate is read. m777 is the document that would name the twelve children. married john gerson eliezar kolbe on 3 april 1843 and was widowed on the same date twenty-five years later. she is the third van der merwe to marry into these families. 15 september 2026 - mccabe has a first name, a birth date and an office. he is francis mccabe, landdrost of bloemfontein, son of dr patrick mccabe, a staff-assistant surgeon attached to the british army on the cape frontier, born at one of the military posts in what is now british kaffraria on 29 september 1817. his obituary in the friend says he "married his second wife about ten months since - the widow of the late commandant j.g.e. kolbe, of kafirberg, near this town", and he died suddenly of heart disease on the modder river road on 23 february 1872, aged 54, leaving "a widow, four sons and two daughters, besides a large family of step-children". so: married 3 april 1843, widowed 3 april 1868 with twelve children, married again about april 1871, widowed again fifteen months later, and dead in 1896 under his name. for about eleven months there were eighteen children attached to one household. she was living at springfield, ward upper modder-river, district bloemfontein in october 1868, when a black mare and foal of hers were stolen - the court record that says so is the only document this archive has that shows her doing anything at all.

his mother rose died at bloemfontein on 1 august 1858, aged 72 years 3 months and 8 days. he married anna jacoba van der merwe about april 1871 - "his second wife, about ten months since" - and was dead within fifteen months. on the anniversary of the state's independence he had spent the day superintending the burghers' annual target shooting for the government prize; it is the best kind of source and it is not a register. 1820 settler - the nautilus, owen's party, algoa bay 14 apr 1820. married at sixteen on a sworn falsehood, and the roll carries a second one: "kolbe, george augustus 20. chemist. w margaret 19", where he was sixteen and she was sixteen. he sailed from gravesend four days before his seventeenth birthday. the two lies do not even agree - nobody "twenty-one and upwards" in january 1819 is twenty in december. owen's party was 52 people, no. 3 on the colonial department list, joint-stock and recruited in london, and it collapsed in 1821 when thomas owen refused to draw rations and left; his brother took over and the party dispersed. he was eighteen, with no leader, no rations and no location, and the next record of him is the graaff-reinet mission three years later. preached across the orange river. his grandson could not name him in 1915. 15 september - he was an lms missionary, and his father wrote to him. the south african library at cape town holds msb751, the ga kolbe collection, donated by dr jean griffiths of somerset west in 1985: "george augustus kolbe, pharmacist, 1820 settler, missionary, married margaret downing" and, on a second entry, "george augustus kolbe, 1802-44. lms missionary." it corroborates a memory this archive published the same morning as an inference - john montgomery's recollection of a bushman mission school at koolskop about 1824, where colesberg now stands. two sources with nothing to do with each other, agreeing. the collection is four photocopied pages containing a letter of 23 august 1830 from johan kolbe in london to his son - the only known document connecting the tailor of conduit street to the settler of colesberg. it has now been read, and it does not carry a street address. the catalogue called it a letter "on his ordination" and this archive repeated the catalogue; it is not. 20 september 2026 - and a second attachment came with it. a two-page afrikaans typescript headed "msb 751 / [konsep] vir dsab / voorlopige teks", initialled ks and dated 18/2/92 - a draft entry for the dictionary of south african biography, by dr karel schoeman, on the word of the national library that holds the file: "the author, ks, would be dr. karel schoeman who worked here at the national library". it is a secondary work and this archive does not take secondary works as evidence - but it agrees with this archive on nine points reached by nine other roads (the 1802 birth, j.g.e. kolbe 1822-68 at leeuberg as a commandant, margaret downing 1803-1867, the 1819 london marriage, the apothecary's trade, the farm wurthemberg, ten children, philippolis from march 1831) and it is wrong about exactly one thing: it calls his father a german apothecary. he was a tailor, on 121 rate books, two printed masters' lists, three gazette notices, the census, the burial register and his other son's sworn deposition. the trade is the son's, moved one generation up. what the entry adds, all of it untested: the graaff-reinet missionary society from about 1824, working among the slaves of the district; acceptance as an lms mission assistant on 8 february 1828 and posting to boesmanskool - the present bethulie - with james clark among the san; a journey with melvill to the caledon valley in november 1828, as far as present-day ladybrand, the earliest journey in the present free state of which a written record survives, and printed under his own name in the transactions of the missionary society for 1829 - a second document he wrote himself, searched for and not found; philippolis from march 1831, alone after melvill left in march 1832; ordination on 25 may 1833 by the french missionaries arbousset and casalis; his advice behind the berlin missionary society's founding of bethanie in 1834; an accusation of adultery in 1836 with the wife of one of his congregation, agitated by h. hendricks, secretary of the griqua council - an inquiry by the french missionaries acquitted him - continued opposition from t. atkinson, withdrawal from the station in march 1837 and dismissal by the lms on 19 june 1837; and the farm driefontein near philippolis. it is also wrong a second time, and in its own first source: it says his death notice records only eight children. the death notice names ten, and this archive has read it, photographed it and published the transcription - kab mooc 6/9/35: 7698, signed m. kolbe at colesberg in january 1845. it also settles the farm name. this archive had wirtemberg from the obituary and knapdaar from the death notice and had quietly run them into one address; "wurthemberg, sometimes also given as knapdaar" is the statement that assumption needed. and it names a portrait: a likeness of him as a young man, in 1992 with c.j. du plessis of ruigtevlei, district bethulie, reproduced in olivier (1973); and a charles bell watercolour of a church service at philippolis in 1834 with kolbe in the pulpit, in the africana museum, johannesburg. this archive holds no likeness of anybody born before 1850. there may be two of this man. and he wrote something else, and it is findable. the 1829 journal extract the dsab cites is catalogued under the other man's name, which is why a search for kolbe found nothing: "extracts of the journal of messrs melvill and kolbe, addressed to the rev. richard miles, superintendent of the society's missions in africa, philippolis, 25 nov. 1828", in the council for world missions archive at soas - which is source 4 on the dsab's own list, two lines above source 6. an edited version dated 18 november 1828 appears in melvill (1829), and the journey is printed entire in karel schoeman (ed.), early white travellers in the transgariep, 1819-1840 (protea, 2003), p. 30. legassick quotes him: on the caledon they met people with "no other means of subsistence than the wild animals found in these parts". the first words of his this archive has read, and they are about famine. and the man he addressed it to is very probably the man who called at his father's house: richard miles was sent to cape town to act as dr philip's substitute while philip was in england, which puts him at the cape in 1828 and back in london by 1830. the 1830 letter says only "mr miles", so this is an identification and not a document. 20 september, later - and the society's own register has him, free, in eight lines. james sibree, a register of missionaries (lms, 4th ed. 1923), entry 278: "was previously connected with the graaff reinet missionary society, and laboured among the slaves around graaff reinet. was accepted provisionally by mr. miles, feb. 8, 1829, which action was confirmed by the directors, july 29, 1829. first laboured with mr. clark, at the bushman station, caledon river. thence proceeded to philippolis, arriving there, march 13, 1831. on may 26, 1833, he was ordained by the french missionaries, messrs. lemue, pellisier, and arbousset. his connection was dissolved by the directors, june 19, 1837." it settles mr miles - the man who called at the tailor's house in london was no messenger, he was the officer who accepted him - and it explains the father's adverb, because "provisionally" by miles and "confirmed" by the directors is precisely what "fully accepted" means. it disagrees with the dsab on the year of acceptance (1829, not 1828), the day of the ordination (26 may) and the men who performed it (lemue, pellissier and arbousset - no casalis). and it is wrong about a son. entry 522 calls frederick william kolbe, the rhenish then lms missionary of george and paarl, "son of rev. g. a. kolbe (no. 278)", where schoeman says he was no relation. schoeman is right and the society's own register is wrong: the arithmetic gave it away - a birth of 3 november 1821 against john gerson eliezar's 7 july 1822, eight months apart - and three works settled it. the new catholic encyclopedia calls his son monsignor f.c. kolbe "the son of a westphalian (german) protestant missionary"; s2a3 names him friedrich wilhelm kolbe, herero scholar, married at cape town in 1849 and at okahandja by april 1850; and the dsab had published its own entry on him in 1987. sibree has two kolbes in south africa and a compiler joined them. and his own journals are catalogued, in london. the council for world mission archive at soas, item-level: cwm/lms/05/05/100 - "extracts from the journal of john melvill and george augustus kolbe, during a tour to the north-eastwards of philippolis, 13-22 nov 1828", the manuscript behind the printed extract this archive hunted all morning; /102, extracts at philippolis 1828-1831; /106, journal, philippolis 1831-1834; /108, journal, philippolis 6 oct 1832 - sep 1833. six years of his life in his own writing, where this archive has held one sentence of his at second hand. and the year of the accusation is one box: incoming correspondence /044 (1835, which the catalogue says contains him), /046 (1836) and the 1837 file - 1836-1837 is box 15. and one likeness is catalogued, in scotland: university of edinburgh, centre for the study of world christianity, cswc 60 - five photograph copies of bell sketches of african congregations, item 3 "mr. kolbe… at philippolis in 1834". edinburgh calls him "a moravian missionary?", question mark and all; he was london missionary society, and this archive has his father's letter saying so. the dsab puts the original watercolour in johannesburg and never mentions scotland; edinburgh never mentions johannesburg.

q: stephanus francois booyzen c. oct 1874, cape province - 14 may 1940, east lynne, pretoria · booyzen the stone is now read, and it is the fullest document this archive has for him. silverton, pretoria, a double stone under one base reading booyzen: "'n simbool van liefde - aan my dierbare eggenoot en ons vader - stefanus francois - ✳ 29-9-1874, † 14-5-1940 - sy plek is leeg, sy stem is stil, ons swyg o'heer, dit is gods wil. ges. 75:1". his birth is now exact: 29 september 1874, where this archive had only "c. october 1874". and a pillar between the two halves lists twelve children by their household names - ouboet · ousie · bessie · betie · henna · evert · ✝baba · fanie · willie · pietie · johan · hennie - one of them marked dead with a cross. this archive had almost none of them. they are nicknames, not names on a register, and nothing is claimed from them beyond the count. his grave is found and photographed: "booyzen stefanus francois 1874-1940", silverton main cemetery, pretoria - a joint stone with his wife, "booyzen beatrix magdalena catharina nee boshoff 1889-1977". both dates match this archive exactly, and hers is the first death year it has had for her. he died at east lynne, pretoria, and lies at silverton. image located, not yet read. prisoner of war. a printed transport list in the pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries three consecutive booyzens shipped on the city of cambridge on 3 june 1901, all entered from pretoria: 18463 stephanus francois, 28 · 18464 petrus jacobus, 29 · 18465 david schalk, 54. consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. age 28 against this archive's c. october 1874, which would have made him 26. the fuller register was then found, and it is better than the de list in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at pretoria, riding with the pretoria commando, and taken at tolosberg on 25 april 1901. its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the de list's 28, 29 and 54 did not. and then the prisoner number led somewhere else entirely. the medal-roll database at angloboerwar.com holds an entry for a stephanus francois booysen, burger, whose pow number is 18463 - the same number as the register - and it says he was a zarp, one of the zar's police, based at pretoria. quoting a city coins auction catalogue of november 2020 that described his abo medal and the papers with it: in action at talana, modder spruit, colenso, platrand (wagon hill) where he was wounded in the right leg above the knee, spion kop and dalmanutha - the zarps' famous last stand. his applications were completed by his commanding officer, commandant j. p. de la c. schroeder. he was one of forty-two boers taken at tolosberg in the waterval valley on 25 april 1901, with two guns and much stock, and was sent to india. this archive has not seen the medal or the application; it is strong secondary evidence tied to the register by the number and not by the name. what it does to the dispute: he is numbered 18463 and david schalk booysen is 18465, two apart on the same transport on the same day, and this man died at east lynne, pretoria, which is the district all three were taken in. that is a fourth point favouring david schalk as his father, and the first that does not depend on a forename. it is still not a document naming a parent. parentage disputed - see below. a son of the second marriage, and a messelaar - a mason, like his half-brother willem hermanus at indwe. his 1940 sterfkennis was fetched because it should have named his mother; his widow wrote only "oorlede" for both parents. married beatrix magdalena catharina boshoff at mosselbaai on 5 september 1905, certificate 1318 - he 30 and a jonkman, she sixteen with her parents consenting. eleven children; left immovable property and a will. the register gives his residence as pretoria, and eleven weeks later david schalk booijzen of goede hoop, pretoria - whose 1900 notice names an unmarried major son called stephanus francois - remarried in that same city. this archive placed him under petrus jacobus on his birth year alone. it is marked serious on the disputed page and it is not decided.

q: williem johannes kolbe of panfontein 9 jul 1847, district of philippolis - 1941 - aged about 94 · kolbe taken prisoner in 1901, aged 54, at panfontein in the bloemfontein district, and recorded as a free stater. tna wo 108/368 folio 603. sent to natal. **and on 21 september 2026 the line in the prisoner list got a life.** he is **general willem johannes kolbe (1847-1941)**, who led the **bloemfontein commando** and commanded the southern districts of bloemfontein. **born 9 july 1847 in the district of philippolis** - the place his grandfather preached at, and where charles bell drew a kolbe in the pulpit in 1834. he was at the **siege of kimberley, where he was made general**, and afterwards at **paardeberg, driefontein and the brandwaterkom**, and he rode in **de wet's invasion of the cape colony in february 1901** - the year he was captured. **two horses were shot under him.** the french general de villebois-mareuil spoke of his leadership with praise; he was liked in his commando and is said to have treated the burghers kindly. **the source is printed, not a tree** - but read at one remove, and that is said plainly. the career above is in *afrikanergeskiedenis* (petronel fourie) and on the afrikaans wikipedia. **the pedigree below is on the wikipedia article only**, which cites **p. j. nienaber, *afrikaanse biografiese woordeboek* (voortrekkerpers, 1947), p. 139** and the fourie piece without saying which carries what; the fourie piece was read here in full and has no genealogy in it at all, **so nienaber is the source by elimination and his page has not been seen**. **and it names his house.** father **j. g. e. kolbe**, mother **anna jacoba van der merwe**, grandfather **george augustus kolbe, "a german missionary"**, grandmother **margaret downing**, the grandfather at **knapdaar, burgersdorp**, the home farm **onder-leeuwberg in the bloemfontein district**, and the father **a commandant in the basuto war of 1865**. every one of those is held here already and independently, including the two women's names and the farm the commandant died on. **the 1847 in the prisoner list and the 1847 in the dictionary are the same year, and panfontein and onder-leeuwberg are the same district.** **what is still not proved**: that the man in the prisoner list is the man in the dictionary. two documents agreeing on a name, a year and a district is strong and is not a register. **vab mhg m777**, the widow's 1896 estate, would name all twelve children - and so, in his own words, might *herinneringe van genl. w j kolbe* at the free state archives.

booysens suburb, johannesburg · witwatersrand not a family place - a trap. booysens is a mining suburb south of the johannesburg city centre, a couple of miles from forest hill and kenilworth where this family actually lived in the 1940s. it means every name-index search for booysen in johannesburg returns people whose only connection to the word is an address. the archive met it head-on: a death notice indexed under the surname daschner turned out to belong to charles bruce rennie, a miner of booysens, and nothing else about him touches this family at all. 

brakfontein farm · district rustenburg, transvaal the farm where the oldest document in this archive was written. on 14 september 1876, thirteen days after the death, somebody at brakfontein filled in sterfkennis no. 678 for petrus jacobus booijsen, aged 88, and wrote the names of his parents on line 3. fifteen years later it takes two more: his son's wife on 9 may 1891 and their son five days after her. and in 1892 hendrik stefanus, marrying again at zeerust, still gives brakfontein as his home - sixteen years on the same ground. the coordinates are approximate: the district is certain, the farm is not yet placed. 

lichtenburg district · western transvaal where this family's western transvaal branch is, and it is a branch rather than a lead now. jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen - fifth of the eight children on the 1876 sterfkennis, born district graaff-reinet about 1818 - died on the farm vaalbank in this district on 25 may 1885, estate tab mhg o/2899. his daughter magdalena susanna maria died on the same farm on 1 may 1920, and her sterfkennis names him. lichtenburg is one district west of rustenburg, where his father died in 1876, and one district east of marico. 

dugmore mine colliery · indwe, district wodehouse where a booyzen worked underground. the indwe marriage register of 21 september 1908 gives both bride and groom's dwelling place as "dugmore mijn" and the groom's trade as "mijnwerker". it is the only mine anywhere in this archive attached to a named member of this family, and it is coal in the cape rather than gold on the rand. the coordinates are approximate - the workings were at indwe and the exact site is not yet fixed. 

vaalbank farm · district lichtenburg, transvaal one farm, two deaths, thirty-five years apart, and the same family on it both times. jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen - born district graaff-reinet about 1818, fifth child on the 1876 sterfkennis - died here on 25 may 1885. his daughter magdalena susanna maria, born about 1860, died here on 1 may 1920. it is the clearest evidence this archive has that the family did not merely pass through the western transvaal but settled in it, two generations before anyone reached johannesburg. the coordinates are approximate: the district is certain, the farm is not yet placed. and a school on it. the education files of the south african republic hold a school at vaalbank, district lichtenburg, post office rietkuil, teacher j.p. louw, running through 1898 and 1899 - and the man beside the teacher on its money papers is written ds. booysen and ds booijsen. in february 1899 he wrote to the government to ask how school materials could be provided to orphans, arising from a case among them. whether ds. is a david schalk or the dutch abbreviation for a minister cannot be read off an index line, and six weeks earlier the same school wrote "ds van roojen" in the same slot. 

cherryville farm · district barkly east the third named barry farm, after manorowen and jerpoint. harriet louisa barry, eighteen, died here of typhoid on 7 september 1912 after thirty days' illness and was carried back to manorowen to be buried. her father, who signed the form, gave his own residence as manorowen - so cherryville is somewhere the family worked rather than lived, or another barry household entirely. the coordinates are approximate.

koedoesfontein farm · district rustenburg, transvaal where hendrik stephanus booysen died on 11 may 1908, aged seventy-nine, in the house of his son-in-law willem grobelaar. a farmer with no movable property, some land, and mutual wills with both of his dead wives. thirty-two years earlier he had signed his own father's sterfkennis at brakfontein, one district over. the coordinates are approximate. 

zeerust town, district marico · transvaal the principal town of marico, and the district this archive spent weeks holding at arm's length with the sentence "they are not this family, who were cape". hendrik stefanus booijzen married here on 14 april 1892 - 63, a widower of brakfontein - and signed his second wife's death notice here in august 1902. the sentence is withdrawn.

klerksdorp town · transvaal where ockert johannes stephanus booysen died on 16 january 1921, aged 69 - the man who signed his father's death notice in 1908 and who carried his mother's father's name out of the district of cradock and into the western transvaal. it is a civil registration and it names no parents, which is why this archive keeps going back to sterfkennisse. he has no estate file of his own. 

market street, pretoria street · pretoria, transvaal elizabetha margaretha booijzen, born marais, died in a zinc building in market street on 1 june 1900 - the capital's main street, four days before lord roberts entered the town. her husband david schalk booijzen, the direct ancestor's brother, did not file her death notice for three years and nine months, and against the question about movable property he wrote "none. compensation claim filed." 

turffontein suburb · johannesburg, transvaal 18 anderson street. richard peter booyzen, twenty-four, married, a sawyer, died here of influenza and pneumonia on 25 october 1918 after eleven days - the centre of black october, which killed some fourteen thousand people on the rand in six weeks. he was buried at brixton two days later. his birthplace on the form is the cape of good hope: born in the north-eastern cape, dead in a johannesburg mining suburb at twenty-four. 

mayfair suburb · johannesburg, transvaal this archive has had mayfair as a word on two pages and never as an address. kathleen barry died here in 1940. her great-granddaughter catherine mary sophia booyzen was married at st joseph's, mayfair on 15 january 1949 - the hinge into the lerena archive. and her son henry james booyzen was living at 3 15th avenue when he died in 1956. three generations in one suburb, and the cemetery register is what finally gave it a street number. 

roodepoort town · west rand, transvaal hendrik stephanus nicolaas booysen - baptised at rustenburg in 1882, dead at kempton park in 1959 - was buried in the central cemetery of the municipality of roodepoort-maraisburg on 12 october 1959, section i d.r., entry 96. this archive published him as buried at johannesburg for an afternoon because the familysearch collection carries that title for every register inside it. 

goedehoop place · pretoria, transvaal two men of this story lived here. charles petrus barend lowies, a hawker born in the district of cradock about october 1848, is "of goedehoop, pretoria" on his 1905 death notice - he died in the pretoria lunatic asylum on 5 june that year, leaving twelve children, six still minors. and david schalk booijzen, born in the district of cradock in june 1848, gives goede hoop, pretoria as his home on the register when he marries lowies's widow on 27 november, five months and twenty-two days later. this archive read that register first and wrote the address down without knowing what it meant. coordinates approximate. 

s: Hill, place of capture · Eastern Transvaal
q: tolosberg hill, place of capture · eastern transvaal where three booyzens were taken, and the only place on this map whose position this archive cannot vouch for. stefanus francois, petrus jacobus and david schalk booysen - prisoners 18463, 18464 and 18465, all of pretoria and all of the pretoria commando - were captured here on 25 april 1901, among forty-two boers taken with two guns and much stock. six weeks later they sailed from cape town on the city of cambridge. the hill itself is not on any map this archive has found. it is in no gazetteer reachable by search, in no battle list, and in no day-by-day war diary of 1901; the single source for the name gives only "tolosberg in the waterval valley, eastern transvaal". the pin is therefore placed at waterval boven, in the elands river valley - the waterval valley of the eastern transvaal, and twenty kilometres from dalmanutha, where the same man had fought the previous august. that placement is this archive's inference and not the source's. there is more than one waterval in the transvaal, including one in the lydenburg district north of here, and the hill could as easily be there. jeppe's map of 1899 has now been read and it does not carry the name. sheet 6 of the six-sheet map - the definitive survey of the south african republic, finished the year the war began - was examined over about twenty-five kilometres of the elands river valley either side of this pin, at full resolution. it names every farm with its number: waterval 161, kindergoed, elandshoek, eerste geluk, groot geluk, nooitgedacht, vlakplaats, kaalbosch, schoonspruit, kietspruit, weltevreden, treurfontein, uitkomst - and waterval boven and waterval onder stations on the delagoa bay line, with godwaan station east of them. it also names hills, in the form jeppe used: mauch bg., spitskop, tafel kop, peerds kop, zwart kop, zuikerboschkop, silverkop, vaalkop. there is no tolosberg among them. that does not move the pin and it does not prove the source wrong; it means the name was local, or was spelt otherwise, or was never a surveyed feature. the pin is still an inference - but it is now a tested one. 

knap daar farm · district colesberg the kolbe farm before wurtemburg. a land memorial of 1839 - cape town archives repository, lg 552, reference 664 - records "reverend g kolbe" asking that government ground adjoining his farm knap daar, in the district of colesberg, be surveyed and auctioned. this archive has george augustus kolbe dying at the farm wurtemburg in the same district on 1 december 1844, and knows he preached across the orange river; the memorial styles him reverend five years earlier and gives him land. the identification rests on an initial and a district, not on a full name, and the pin is placed at colesberg because the farm itself is not on any map read here. 

wakkerstroom town and district · eastern transvaal where the settler's family ended up, four hundred miles from the font. george augustus kolbe the 1820 settler died at colesberg in 1844 and is buried at burgersdorp; his son frederik fortunatus baptised eight children at colesberg, hopetown and bethulie between 1863 and 1881; and three of those eight marry or are found at wakkerstroom in the eastern transvaal. the eldest, another george augustus, was born at colesberg on 29 july 1863 and died here on 28 september 1954, aged ninety-one - a man whose life spans the whole of this archive's south african century. two men named george augustus kolbe lived and are buried here, born two years apart - 2 october 1861 and 29 july 1863 - and the older of them was the prisoner of war of 1902. two of his sons died here in 1918 four months apart, which is the influenza, and one of them carried the london surname downing into the eastern transvaal, which is what proved the connection. a woman named angeline kolbe died here on 15 november 1900, aged 28, and this archive cannot say who she was. 

s: Town, and a camp · Eastern Transvaal
q: volksrust town, and a camp · eastern transvaal twenty miles from wakkerstroom, on the natal border. frederik fortunatus downing kolbe married here. this archive also put a child's grave here for half a day and has taken it back: martha angeline kolbe, sixty days old, is buried at wakkerstroom, and the index that said volksrust was naming the district, which wakkerstroom lies inside. volksrust held one of the concentration camps, and the naairs index holds a camp grave for a g.e. kolbe, aged 35 - which is not the angeline kolbe who died at wakkerstroom in 1900, a different age in a different year in a different town. no person in this archive is yet shown to have been in that camp. 

s: Town, capital of the Orange Free State · Orange Free State
q: bloemfontein town, capital of the orange free state · orange free state the town the commandant's whole public life was attached to, and it took this archive until today to give it a pin. john gerson eliezar kolbe was a director of the bloemfontein bank, a justice of the peace, commandant of this district and a deacon of its dutch reformed church; he advertised a lost promissory note for £154 sterling on its market square in march 1864; he sat as foreman of the jury in a forgery trial here in 1866, before mr van soelen. his farm lay about two hours' ride away. and the man the free state estate index hides his widow behind was this town's own landdrost. francis mccabe, born at a frontier military post on 29 september 1817, son of dr patrick mccabe of the british army on the cape frontier, married anna jacoba van der merwe about april 1871 and was dead by 23 february 1872, of heart disease on the modder river road after a cart went into a sluit in the moonlight. he was buried here on the sunday afternoon at six o'clock, the coffin carried from the house by the resident members of the volksraad and the principal government officers, with the state president and upwards of two hundred people walking behind. 

s: Mission station, later town · Southern Orange Free State
q: philippolis mission station, later town · southern orange free state where the settler's children grew up, on the word of a man writing in 1868 who knew them. the obituary of commandant john gerson eliezar kolbe says his father "became a missionary to the griquas at philippolis, and most of his family, we believe, grew up there". this archive had reached the same conclusion from the children's baptism places - harriet hachilah machilah born here in 1831 - and this is a fourth, independent source for it. philippolis was the london missionary society's griqua station; george augustus kolbe was an l.m.s. missionary. 

s: Mission station, later town · Southern Orange Free State
q: bethulie mission station, later town · southern orange free state the other mission on the circuit, and a font this family came back to. frederik fortunatus kolbe was born here in 1839 - the source of a forename that has since crossed into four surnames - and johan casimir in 1844, the year his father died. forty-two years later frederik fortunatus brought his own youngest daughter, adriana henrietta johanna, back to be baptised here on 23 october 1881.

s: Farm · District Bloemfontein, Orange Free State
q: leeuwberg farm · district bloemfontein, orange free state where commandant kolbe died, on the night of friday 3 april 1868, of typhus caught on commando. the pin was at fauresmith and it was wrong. it rested on a 1903 free state land file recording a "leeuwberg no 465, dist. faurismith" - a farm of the right name in the right province thirty-five years later, and nothing more - and it was published with its own objection attached, that fauresmith is a hundred and thirty kilometres from kaalspruit while the obituary says he died at the one and lies at the other. the objection has been answered against the pin. the friend of the free state of 13 january 1870 advertises for sale "the farm, wildebeestkooi, adjoining the farm leeuberg, the property of the late j.g.e. kolbe, about two hours ride from the town of bloemfontein". fifteen or twenty kilometres, not a hundred and thirty. the fauresmith farm is a different farm of the same name, and the two-farm contradiction this archive could not reconcile was never a contradiction - leeuberg and kaalspruit are neighbours. a man named jephts, described by the court as a man of colour, was living here in 1868 and owned a chestnut riding horse; it was stolen with two of the family's, and his name is in the record beside theirs. 

s: Farm · District Bloemfontein, Orange Free State
q: kaalspruit farm · district bloemfontein, orange free state his own address, in his own advertisement. the friend of the free state, 9 march 1864: a lost promissory note, £154 sterling, signed "j.g.e. kolbe, kafferberg, kaalspruit". the obituary of 1868 says he settled here about 1850 and lies buried here. the pin is at bloemfontein and it is an inference: a free state soil-conservation district is registered as "kaalspruit - kafferrivier (bloemfontein)", which pairs the same two names the advertisement pairs, in the district whose bank he was a director of and whose paper he advertised in. a name pair is not a survey beacon. the friend's own transcriber read this farm as "[randspruit]", bracketed and doubtful; the advertisement is why this archive reads kaalspruit. 15 september 2026 - the guess now has three documents behind it. the obituary of his second wife's husband calls him "the late commandant j.g.e. kolbe, of kafirberg, near this town", the town being bloemfontein. an 1870 auction advertisement puts the neighbouring farm leeuberg "about two hours ride from the town of bloemfontein". and his widow was living at springfield, ward upper modder-river, district bloemfontein in october 1868. kafferberg, kaalspruit, leeuberg, wildebeestkooi and springfield are one neighbourhood, and it is not at fauresmith. 

piet retief town · eastern transvaal two kolbe stones, thirty years apart, in a town forty miles from wakkerstroom. "g.a. kolbe, geb. 23 feb. 1836, overl. 7 jan. 1913" with "a.m. kolbe, geb. 4 mei 1843, overl. 21 sep. 1907", raised van hun kinders; and "p.j. kolbe, geb. 1_ aug. 1865, oorl. 28 nov. 1919". 1836 is the year the settler's twins were born at burgersdorp, and if that is him the stone dates a birth this archive has only ever had as a year. 

hoopstad town · orange river colony where the werdmuller line ends up. charles andrew werdmuller - second son of the man who married the settler's fourth daughter - is "charles werdmuller, j.p. of hoopstad" by 1909. his wife charlotte anne, born callaghan, died here on 17 february 1891 aged thirty-two, "after a long illness", having arrived "only a few months ago, in rather indifferent health", of a disorder of the heart that proved organic. she left "a husband and two little girls", and one of those girls married a holder of the victoria cross.
